name: Centro Historico (Mercado dos Tropeiros & Cathedral)
description: The core historic district around the Praca Conselheiro Mata, the Catedral Metropolitana, and the 19th-century Mercado dos Tropeiros market hall. Steep cobbled streets, pastel Baroque townhouses, and the highest concentration of cafes, pousadas, and restaurants in town. This is where most visitors base themselves, walking distance to almost everything but genuinely hilly underfoot.
vibe: colonial, walkable, touristic by day, quiet and musical by night
bestFor: first-time visitors and short-to-medium stays who want everything within walking distance
pros: Walkable to nearly all sights, cafes, and restaurants
Best concentration of laptop-friendly cafes and wifi
Seresta music and evening atmosphere on weekends
cons: Very steep, uneven cobblestones, tough on ankles and luggage
Noisier and pricier during festivals and weekends

name: Bairro Rio Grande (Casa de JK area)
tagline: Quieter streets near the president's childhood home
description: A residential pocket just beyond the busiest tourist core, anchored by the Casa de Juscelino Kubitschek museum, birthplace of Brazil's former president. Streets here are calmer than the main square but still colonial in character, with local bakeries, small mercearias, and a slower pace. A good middle ground between historic charm and everyday residential life.
bestFor: nomads wanting historic character without constant tourist foot traffic
pros: Quieter than the main square while still central
Easy walk to the historic core and museums
More local, less touristy daily life
cons: Fewer cafes and dining options within the immediate blocks
Still hilly, no relief from the cobblestones

name: Palha (Vila Operaria)
tagline: A working residential district beyond the tourist center
description: A largely residential neighborhood a short drive or longer walk from the historic center, home to many Diamantina locals and university-adjacent renters. Housing here is simpler and cheaper than centro properties, with fewer colonial facades and more everyday Brazilian small-town life: local bars, mercados, and modest houses on quieter, sometimes flatter streets.
bestFor: longer stays and budget-focused nomads comfortable being outside the tourist bubble
pros: Noticeably cheaper rents than the historic center
Flatter streets in parts, easier daily walking
cons: Farther from cafes, sights, and the main square
Very little English spoken, fewer tourist services

name: Biribiri
tagline: A former mill village turned nature escape
description: A 19th-century textile village about 12 kilometers outside Diamantina, now largely absorbed into the Biribiri State Park, with old worker houses, a chapel, and river swimming holes surrounded by highland grasslands and quartzite peaks. Not a place to live day to day, but a short drive from town for hiking, swimming, and escaping the historic center's tourist bustle for an afternoon or overnight stay.
bestFor: day trips, hikes, and nomads craving nature immersion outside the main town
pros: Dramatic Serra do Espinhaco scenery and river swimming
Genuinely peaceful, minimal tourist crowds on weekdays
Easy add-on trip from Diamantina without long travel
cons: No real infrastructure for remote work or long stays
Requires a car or organized tour to reach reliably
